patterns.short_summary: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from.
patterns.curator_notes: The final three follow the consensus top three; no score required an adjustment. I retained StepWrite and Socrates above the email example for their broader adaptive mechanisms and higher consequential impact, while recognizing that the email example has the clearest literal structural evidence. Readers should distrust any strong claim that StepWrite or Socrates necessarily asks the very first question before all user content: their excerpts establish adaptive questioning and downstream use, but do not expose the complete turn sequence or input-record schema. The email excerpt clearly establishes system-generated questions and user answers, but only implies rather than explicitly describes how those answers are assembled into the final reply. GenerativeGUI was excluded despite unusually concrete JSON evidence because the excerpt suggests clarification inside an already-started chat, conflicting with the strict head-of-loop signature.

papers.title: Socrates: Data Story Generation via Adaptive Machine-Guided Elicitation of User Feedback
papers.why: Socrates makes the elicitation policy part of generation: the machine adaptively selects questions, records the user's feedback, and incorporates it into the resulting data story. This clearly demonstrates how system-authored questions can progressively determine a generative specification.

papers.title: Understanding and Supporting Formal Email Exchange by Answering AI-Generated Questions
papers.why: The system derives short questions from an incoming email, and the user's answers constitute the specification for a reply instead of requiring the user to compose either a full response or a generative prompt. The source artifact, system questions, user action, and target task are all explicit, making this the cleanest directly reconstructable inversion in the set.

patterns.short_summary: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates.
patterns.curator_notes: I departed from the consensus order by selecting rank 4, DesignWeaver, instead of rank 3, Composable Prompting Workspaces. DesignWeaver more clearly satisfies the defining derivation step: its controls come from generated images, whereas the evidence for Composable Prompting Workspaces establishes dynamic widgets and downstream influence but not artifact-specific extraction or regeneration when the artifact changes. I raised DesignWeaver from 4.27 to 4.40; no adjustment exceeds 0.3. Evidence caveats: GazeNoter’s quotation is truncated, and DesignWeaver’s abstract leaves the exact control-to-regeneration loop and handle regeneration behavior implicit. Even AI-Instruments’ otherwise strong figure evidence does not explicitly state whether its fragment set is automatically regenerated after every input change.

papers.title: GazeNoter: Co-Piloted AR Note-Taking via Gaze Selection of LLM Suggestions to Match Users' Intentions
papers.why: GazeNoter extracts context keywords from the user’s latest spoken sentence, exposes those input-dependent terms for selection, and uses the selections to shape candidate sentences. It is a strong example of replacing repeated free-text specification with a dynamically derived set of discrete handles.

papers.title: AI-Instruments: Embodying Prompts as Instruments to Abstract & Reflect Graphical Interface Commands as General-Purpose Tools
papers.why: The system decomposes an existing image into image-specific prompt fragments, renders those dimensions as individually editable controls, and regenerates the image when a fragment changes. The evidence directly captures the complete derivation–control–downstream-operation chain and makes the content-dependent nature of the controls unusually easy to reconstruct.

patterns.short_summary: Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification.
patterns.curator_notes: I retained the consensus top three and their order after checking the structural signature. I slightly lowered AI-Instruments because its abstract-level quote does not expose the grounding interaction, later execution, or user editability; that third selection is consequently less secure than the first two. GenNI also lacks explicit evidence of later reuse or editing of the inferred control states. Ripplet has the strongest evidence, although the supplied quote still does not explicitly say whether users can inspect or revise the inferred command. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3.

papers.title: Codesigning Ripplet: an LLM-Assisted Assessment Authoring System Grounded in a Conceptual Model of Teachers' Workflows
papers.why: A manual edit to one finished question is interpreted, generalized into a reusable edit command, and applied to other questions—the clearest complete demonstration-to-operative-specification loop in the candidates.

patterns.short_summary: An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on.
patterns.curator_notes: I promoted GANSpiration from third to first because its quote most completely exposes the structural signature: artifact ingestion, latent encoding, and downstream transformation. I retained CareerCraft but placed it second because its uploaded-document path is strong while its free-text reflections may have been produced for the workflow. I selected the immersive-memory system over consensus runner-up TubeLens: TubeLens is conceptually compelling, but its high rater spread and missing import/consent and inference details make it weaker as a reconstructable structural exemplar. Readers should also distrust any implication that the available quotes fully document the interfaces: GANSpiration’s quote omits the later generation controls, CareerCraft does not distinguish pre-existing from workflow-authored reflections, and the immersive-memory quote does not specify its capture or upload interaction.

papers.title: CareerCraft: Supporting New Graduates on Job Hunting with LLM-Assisted Self-Construction of Career Profile
papers.why: CareerCraft exposes a concrete ingestion-and-transformation pipeline in which user-uploaded documents and prior reflections are processed by an LLM into predefined experience cards, turning material the user already has into structured generative output.

patterns.short_summary: A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance.
patterns.curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by promoting rid 15614 from fourth to second and excluding third-ranked rid 5199. CoBRA’s quote proves that users specify a bias value on a 0–4 scale, but it does not show that the value is surfaced as a persistent control widget or that changing it re-runs generation; it therefore demonstrates the subject matter more clearly than the full structure. ImaginationVellum remains selected for design-space coverage, but its evidence is compressed and does not explicitly describe the interaction-and-rerender sequence. TaleBrush’s figure evidence similarly does not state regeneration verbatim, while rid 15614 has the strongest end-to-end evidence. No selected score was adjusted by more than 0.3 from its consensus mean.

papers.title: Steering AI-driven Personalization of Scientific Text for General Audiences
papers.why: The system presents a named 0–100 personalization slider and explicitly generates scientific-text translations at the selected degree, almost exactly reproducing the structural signature.

patterns.short_summary: Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds.
patterns.curator_notes: The final selection retains the consensus top three; no score was adjusted by more than 0.3. The main evidentiary weakness is that none of the excerpts explicitly proves every requirement of the strict signature: system-wide invariance, non-editability, and universal availability on every unit. This uncertainty is smallest for rid 7932. Jamplate does not conclusively show that every competitor or column receives all three questions, and LADICA neither names the relation-type vocabulary nor explicitly confirms that it is identical across all notes. These are therefore structural exemplars based on the supplied interface descriptions, not definitive proof of exact Cartesian completeness.

papers.title: Jamplate: Exploring LLM-Enhanced Templates for Idea Reflection
papers.why: Jamplate exposes three prepared reflection questions and makes each directly invocable: clicking a question generates an answer grounded in the competitor or column being examined. The fixed choices and resulting action–unit binding are unusually concrete and reproducible.

patterns.short_summary: The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification.
patterns.curator_notes: The selected set matches the consensus top three, but Component-Wise Sketching is promoted above CrossLit because its center-distance rule more completely proves the structural signature; this is only a rank departure, and no score adjustment exceeds 0.3. CanvasPic has the strongest evidence because its quote explicitly connects spatial distance to generative influence. Readers should be more cautious with CrossLit: the supplied evidence proves grouping-to-section generation but does not establish an unbounded canvas, free positioning, or sensitivity to coordinates within a group. The Component-Wise Sketching evidence clearly proves positional selection, although the quote alone does not explicitly establish that the surface is unbounded. The selected systems are distinct. Editorial addition: 13801 was added by hand as an additional example; the raters scored it 4.12 and it did not displace a selected exemplar.

papers.title: ImaginationVellum: Generative-AI Ideation Canvas with Spatial Prompts, Generative Strokes, and Ideation History
papers.why: The whole 2D canvas is the prompt: strokes, placement and spatial relationships between elements are read as specification rather than as decoration around a text box. It is the fullest statement of the pattern in the candidate pool, since the canvas is not a staging area whose contents are later serialised into a prompt but is itself the active prompt space. Any tool with a freeform surface can adopt the move of treating arrangement as instruction.

Readers should treat all three mappings as supported by very short abstract/figure excerpts rather than complete interaction descriptions; AI Kitchen’s quote is broad but does not prove every kitchen term has a strict one-to-one system correspondence, and PromptPaint is especially underspecified at that level.

Evidence for rid 3819 is especially narrow because it comes from a figure caption, while the CatAlyst and ProMemAssist excerpts do not independently establish how reliably their triggers work or whether users welcomed the interventions.

papers.title: Are We On Track? AI-Assisted Active and Passive Goal Reflection During Meetings

That internal-decision-to-output edge precisely matches the structural signature, and the structured prompt demonstrates proactive support as an actionable checkpoint rather than a generic alert.

patterns.short_summary: The system emits its output in step with an activity that is unfolding independently — a conversation, a performance, a learning session, a walk through an environment — so that each output appears at the moment its referent occurs.
patterns.curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by excluding its second-ranked candidate, Graphologue (rid 13531), and promoting GestureCoach and StoryDrawer. Although Graphologue strongly demonstrates incremental, no-batch stream processing, its referent is the system’s own GPT-4 response rather than the independently unfolding conversation, performance, learning session, or environmental activity required by the definition. GestureCoach was slightly increased from 4.40 to 4.50 because its quote provides the clearest structural evidence: continuously tracked speech, proactive cues, and delivery during rehearsal. No adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust implementation-level certainty across all three picks: the supplied excerpts establish synchronicity or real-time behavior but do not document timestamp assignment, latency budgets, segmentation granularity, or measured end-to-end delay.

patterns.short_summary: A persistent region sits beside the surface the user is working on and shows generated content derived from that surface's current state.
patterns.curator_notes: The final selection retains the consensus top three, but Marco’s score is reduced slightly because the quoted evidence does not explicitly establish persistent spatial adjacency or read-only status. The strongest two picks have direct evidence for placement and live updating; however, GPTFootprint’s output is calculated telemetry rather than generative prose, so readers should treat it as a structural exemplar rather than a prototypical content-generation case. Marco is the least secure pick: its automatic cross-view derivation is clear, but co-presence is inferred from the named views rather than demonstrated by the quote. Plotania was not promoted despite its novelty because its evidence does not establish the authored source, automatic edit-to-refresh dependency, or side-panel placement; DiagLink was not promoted because its right-hand display may be a structured record of collected information rather than running generated commentary.

papers.title: Beyond Text Generation: Supporting Writers with Continuous Automatic Text Summaries
papers.why: Continuously recomputed paragraph summaries appear as margin annotations beside the text being authored, making the source, automatic derivation, adjacency, and non-committal commentary role explicit.

papers.title: InsightLens: Augmenting LLM-Powered Data Analysis With Interactive Insight Management and Navigation

patterns.short_summary: The system detects something during an ongoing activity but withholds any response until the activity has ended, then presents its findings and the user's controls in a dedicated step.
patterns.curator_notes: The consensus ordering is retained, but all three scores are reduced because none fully demonstrates the complete structural signature, especially findings paired with controls that retroactively revise phase-one material. PRISM receives the largest adjustment, from 2.40 to 2.10, because one rater’s structural disqualification is persuasive: post-task reflection alone is not deferred intervention. Readers should distrust any inference beyond the quoted evidence: 9513 is supported only by an abstract excerpt, TeamVision only by a brief abstract statement, and PRISM only by a figure caption. TeamVision’s silent accumulation is inferred rather than shown, while PRISM’s during-task detection is not evidenced at all. The fourth candidate was excluded because it solicits feedback after the meeting rather than revealing an intervention generated and withheld during it.

papers.title: TeamVision: An AI-powered Learning Analytics System for Supporting Reflection in Team-based Healthcare Simulation
papers.why: Its post-simulation analytics dashboard plausibly creates the pattern’s two phases: an uninterrupted simulation followed immediately by a dedicated debrief using information derived from that simulation. The supplied evidence, however, does not explicitly confirm silent observation or retroactive controls.

papers.title: PRISM: Post-task Reflection via Intelligent Social Multi-agents for Enhancing Learning Experience and Industrial Skill Retention
papers.why: PRISM clearly reserves its assistance for a post-task phase and restructures the completed experience into reflective dialogue, but the evidence does not establish during-task detection, intentional withholding, or controls that revise phase-one material.

patterns.short_summary: Rather than an always-on stream, the system packages interaction into episodes with a defined opening and close.
patterns.curator_notes: I retained the consensus ordering and excluded StayFocused. Its evidence describes sessions set by users, which directly conflicts with the definition’s system-imposed boundary and resembles a focus timer more than a bounded interaction flow. I reduced Poet-Weaver from 2.43 to 2.25 and HINT from 1.83 to 1.55 because neither excerpt confirms the required terminal state or session-scoped reference behavior; neither adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should treat Poet-Weaver and especially HINT as provisional exemplars: their evidence names sessions but does not expose the complete structural signature. StorySage is the only selection whose excerpt directly says that a flow defines one session, though even it lacks evidence for opening, closure, repetition, and cross-session scoping.

papers.title: StorySage: Conversational Autobiography Writing Powered by a Multi-Agent Framework
papers.why: StorySage is the strongest structural match because it explicitly defines its depicted interaction flow as one session, indicating that autobiographical conversation is organized as a bounded episode rather than an always-open thread. The available excerpt does not establish the session’s entry condition, terminal state, or cross-session reference rules, so the exemplar is strong but incompletely evidenced.

patterns.short_summary: A generated continuation is produced at the user's current position in the artifact being edited, and only when the user fires a control to ask for it.
patterns.curator_notes: I reversed the top two consensus candidates: rid 2002 ranks first because its quote directly establishes every critical structural element—explicit invocation, current-caret placement, and the same editing surface—while rid 14006 only strongly implies same-surface cursor-relative insertion. Otherwise, the selected set follows the consensus top three, and no score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust the exact insertion semantics for HiLDE because they are implied rather than stated verbatim. FigurA11y is the weakest inclusion: its figure caption names Generate at Cursor and locates it in the authoring workflow, but does not explicitly describe the activating gesture, whether generation occurs only on request, or how text is committed.

papers.why: This is the most complete structural match: pressing Tab explicitly requests generation, and the suggestion appears after the current caret in the same text editor.

patterns.short_summary: A structure declared in advance — a schema, slot set, section skeleton, or typed taxonomy — determines the form the model's output must take.
patterns.curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by moving rid 623 from fifth to second and excluding consensus runner-up rid 6089. IntelliCircos received a +0.27 adjustment because its quoted evidence most fully exposes a reconstructable structural signature: named types, delimiters, nesting, cardinality, separation, and ordering. Rid 9312 received a small uplift because the template is visibly selected before generation and determines section-level output. Rid 6089 was excluded because its quote establishes a JSON field contract but does not show per-field rendering, validation, rejection, or correction; it is valid but comparatively close to ordinary structured-response formatting. Readers should distrust any stronger claims about validation or downstream rendering for all three picks: none of the supplied excerpts explicitly documents rejection or correction of nonconforming outputs, and the rendering implication is strongest—but still partly inferred—for IntelliCircos. The evidence for rid 5176 also establishes schema extraction and reuse more clearly than it establishes enforcement during every generation.

It is a particularly strong exemplar because the template captures the structure of reasoning itself, not merely the formatting of a response.

No adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should distrust claims about add/edit/remove/reorder operations and cross-generation persistence unless confirmed in the full papers: the supplied evidence consists of short abstract or introduction excerpts and does not directly document those details. ConstitutionMaker is the strongest pick, although even its excerpt does not explicitly show list operations or priority handling.

papers.title: Semantic Commit: Helping Users Update Intent Specifications for AI Memory at Scale

I excluded rid 9046 because “generating and conversing with” personas describes potentially separate stages and therefore does not demonstrate authoring the persona through dialogue. Readers should treat even rid 3352 as a weakly evidenced exemplar rather than a canonical one; the supplied abstract sentence cannot verify the pattern’s decisive feedback loop.

papers.title: CharacterMeet: Supporting Creative Writers' Entire Story Character Construction Processes Through Conversation with LLM-Powered Chatbot Avatars
papers.why: CharacterMeet directly instantiates an artifact under construction—the story character—as an in-character chatbot avatar and uses conversation to support constructing that character, although the evidence does not confirm that replies update its specification or that dialogue is the only authoring surface.
